_comment: The dated release credentials, declared once so something can read them.
§6 states these expiries in prose and called the first of them 'a
renewal date rather than a fact to forget'. Nothing read it, which is §9's
own defect one packaging over: a cadence that is prose is not a cadence.
`expires` is the DECLARED date. `verifyFrom` names the artifact that
actually carries it, and credential-expiry.mjs reads notAfter out of that
artifact whenever it is reachable and FAILS on any drift from the
declaration. Declaring without measuring is exactly how expected-artifacts
.txt certified half-built releases; a hand-maintained date file
Paths are `~`-relative on purpose: the release machine is where this
material lives, and CI has none of it. There, the tool checks the declared
dates and says in as many words that it could not measure them.
The exceptions are K1 and TAG-KEY, whose PUBLIC keys are committed, so
their rows are `./`-relative (resolved against the repository root, never
the cwd) and are measured everywhere gpg is installed, CI included.

credentials.what: Developer ID Application certificate: signs the direct-download macOS build
credentials.breaks: every macOS direct-download release. Builds still sign with an expired leaf and Gatekeeper rejects them on every user's machine, which is a silent-at-build, loud-at-install failure
credentials.note: issued under Apple's G1 Developer ID CA, which itself expires at this exact second, so this date cannot be extended by a reissue under the same authority: the replacement comes from G2

credentials.what: Apple Distribution certificate: signs the Mac App Store app
credentials.breaks: the Mac App Store lane (§13). A store build cannot be signed, so no submission is possible

credentials.what: 3rd Party Mac Developer Installer certificate: signs the store .pkg
credentials.breaks: the Mac App Store lane at the package step specifically. K18 can sign the app perfectly and the .pkg still cannot be produced: they are two certificates and both are required

credentials.what: Mac App Store provisioning profile P9CWZT978L
credentials.breaks: the Mac App Store build. A profile names its certificates and dies with them, so a K18/K19 reissue requires recreating this too

credentials.what: Mac Developer provisioning profile PWABR9JC49, for the §13 hardware-signer proof
credentials.breaks: the WebHID-under-sandbox proof (frontier row 13), which is the check that decides whether the store channel ships at all

credentials.what: release-signing OpenPGP key: signs every RELEASE_HASHES manifest (the earlier of its certify-only primary and its signing subkey)
credentials.breaks: every release lane at once. The ceremony's detached signature over the manifest fails, and every verifier (verify.sh, cws-upload.mjs, the desktop updater, the feed sweep) reports an expired-key signature
credentials.note: installed desktop builds embed a copy of this public key, and that copy carries the old expiry. Renewal is extending the expiry with the offline primary, publishing the refreshed key AND shipping a wallet update that carries it, all before this date, which is why this row's lead time is 180 days rather than the policy's 60

credentials.what: release tag-signing OpenPGP key: every release tag must carry its signature, checked by release.yml's verify-tag step before any job runs
credentials.breaks: every release lane at once. The verify-tag gate no longer yields a usable VALIDSIG for the pinned fingerprint, so no release job runs
credentials.note: renewal is extending the expiry with the offline private key and committing the refreshed tools/release/tag-signing-key.asc, with this row's expires updated in the same commit or the clock reports drift. No wallet update is needed. A rotation instead changes the key file, tag-signing-fingerprint.txt and this row together
